evidence.location: R0.5, section 0, lines 71-74; risk table row 1, lines 257-258
evidence.observation: R0.5 writes: 'Anything GO1 remembers is keyed by the sha256 of the bytes it was computed from and is dropped when the command returns.' The §6 risk control repeats: 'the key is the sha256 of the bytes each caller already holds'. But src/gnd/model/_parsing.py:37 selects the strict JSON reader when 'Path(source).suffix == ".json" or text.lstrip().startswith("{")', and lines 46-49 refuse '{...'-prefixed bytes that are not valid JSON only when the source suffix is .json, falling through to the YAML reader otherwise — so identical bytes under different source names can legitimately parse differently or refuse differently (a .json-named load of '{a: 1}' raises ModelLoadError; the same bytes under a .yaml name load fine). §2 GO1 (lines 145-148) correctly states the cache returns the document 'for the same bytes and the same reader', and the GO1 draft spec's H5 row says the key accounts for the reader, so an implementer following §2 is safe.

concerns.recommendation: Amend R0.5 and the §6 risk row to state the key as (sha256 of bytes, reader identity) — the reader the source name selects — so the binding rule matches §2 and the spec; a bytes-only key would change refusals for '{...'-but-non-JSON bytes in a .json workspace model, which GO1-C2's '.json model' case would catch only after the fact.
concerns.title: R0.5 states the cache key as content sha256 only; reader selection also depends on source name

evidence.location: GO2-C1, section 4, line 228; H11, section 1, line 101
evidence.observation: GO2-C1 requires a refused operation preview 'with its verdict, exit 3', but H11 of the same plan states the refusal's 'exit code and whether the message names an element were not re-read here; the GO2 spec reads them'. At the checkout the refusal-to-exit mapping is message-family based (_evolve_service_exit, src/gnd/evolve/cli_service.py:237-…, reached from the generic EvolutionError arm at :494-495), so the band a candidate-validation refusal lands in is exactly the unverified half of H11 and cannot be assumed to be 3.

concerns.recommendation: Either read the exit code now and cite it in H11, or word GO2-C1 as 'the exit code today's identical refusal produces' so the criterion does not pin an unverified constant the spec phase may have to amend.
concerns.title: GO2-C1 pins exit 3 while H11 says the exit code was not re-read

evidence.location: section 3 order sentence, lines 204-206; GO4 row of the section 3 table, line 201
evidence.observation: The order sentence says 'GO4 at any point after its ruling', but the GO4 row of the same section states its need as 'VG2 and VG5 of reviewed-vocabulary-growth merged or not started (H21)', and H21 (line 111) plus the 'Other writers' paragraph (lines 208-215) impose one writer at a time on unattended-growth.md in the order VG1, GO1, VG2-VG5, then GO2-GO5. Read literally, 'at any point' licenses GO4 concurrent with VG2/VG5, which the plan's own one-writer control forbids.

concerns.recommendation: Qualify the order sentence to 'GO4 at any point after its ruling, once unattended-growth.md is free per the GO4 row's VG2/VG5 straddle condition', so the two statements in the same section cannot be read against each other.
concerns.title: Section 3's 'GO4 at any point' omits the VG2/VG5 one-writer straddle stated in its own table

summary: Plan r2 reviewed against the checkout (HEAD 11a7ebf7; src/tests/docs identical to the cited 548b9a1d). Every code citation read was accurate: _load_model_document's three parses (service.py:264/277/291), the 22/6 parse counts' caller sites (:1507-1518, :1594, :2145, :2203, :2344, :2532, :2539), _parsing.py:25-56, input_policy.py guard_yaml, models.py schema versions and PolicyIssue, discover/output.py candidate_document/candidate_text, shapes.py, model_index.py index_scope, unattended-growth.md lines 235/286/57-73, and all nine §9 lane test files exist. No caller of parse_model_document mutates its return (json_document builds fresh plain dicts, _merge deep-clones, parse_declarations/bytes_declare_includes are read-only), so GO1's shared-document design with the GO1-C3 scope-close canonical comparison is safe as written; R0.2/R0.3 hold. Criteria are falsifiable; GO1-C5 is a same-machine ratio with 2x margin (0.31 vs 0.6) and the plan labels which gates read clocks. Order is acyclic and consistent with the one-writer rule of H21. Three non-blocking concerns: R0.5 and the §6 risk table state the cache key as content-sha256 only, omitting the reader dimension that _parsing.py:37,46-49 shows is selected by source name (§2 and the GO1 spec state it correctly, and GO1-C2's .json case would catch a bytes-only key); GO2-C1 pins exit 3 while H11 defers the exit code to the spec; §3's 'GO4 at any point after its ruling' omits the VG2/VG5 one-writer constraint stated in its own table.
